explanatory_strength.rationale: Round-two re-audit of the frozen packet confirms the same cash-conversion and RPO mechanics as round one. Competitive advantage remains workflow lock-in plus Experience contracts, with generative-AI risk parked in an explicit reserve rather than ignored.

evidence_sufficiency.rationale: Targeted research loop left seat-cohort and Firefly attach unresolved and confirmed segment FCF is still revenue-weighted. Evidence is enough to vote watch, not enough to promote accumulate.

downside_control.rationale: Contract low ~$350/sh versus $234.74 still shows large equity de-rating risk if seats stall. Cash conversion bounds solvency; it does not bound multiple compression from AI competition.

return_vs_alternatives.rationale: Contract base ~15.8% annualized clears a soft hurdle but is not uniquely attractive versus other pricing-power software once AI defense spend and SBC are reserved. Lawrence ~32% remains too optimistic to size on.

claims.claim: Research response confirms seat-cohort and Firefly attach remain unresolved in the frozen packet; management_facts is empty.
FY2025 free cash flow $9.85B ($23.07/sh) and RPO $22.52B remain the primary filing anchors for competitive-advantage cash conversion.

strongest_counter_explanation: H1 acceleration and RPO already embed AI defense success; unresolved cohort data is noise and mid-teens contract return understates durable franchise reinvestment.
most_important_missing_fact: Digital Media net new seats and generative-AI credit attach by cohort.
falsifiers: Two consecutive quarters where RPO growth lags revenue growth
Trailing four-quarter free cash flow per share below $18.00
Documented sustained decline in Digital Media net new ARR with rising competitor seat wins
specialist_findings: Hohn round two: research loop did not close the competitive-advantage evidence gap. Keep watch; do not size on Lawrence synthesis while seat/AI attach remain unverified.
